updates.note: Reported live from a shelter position near the downtown bayfront as Rafael made landfall (arc beat: live from the bayfront).
At landfall (about 1:40 a.m. Tuesday) told Harborline 6: "This is the surge we have been warning about, and it is happening now"; urged people to stay put and not go look at the water.
Wrote the Ledger's lead landfall story with Ellie Navarro (arc beat: lead landfall story).
Morning after landfall: urged residents who stayed home to stay put; "We will get to people, but the wind has to come down first."
Day of landfall: said the surge "came in about where we said it would, and it came in high"; NWS put the surge at about 11 feet, within its 9-12 ft forecast.

First statement after landfall: plant lost both power feeds, pumps damaged, pressure low; apologized ("we're sorry") and asked residents to conserve; said the utility would announce right away if a boil-water notice became necessary (none in effect Tuesday morning).

Day of landfall: confirmed a report of oil discharging from two vessels moored at an Inner Harbor terminal as the storm arrived; no volume, no cause; responders could not get on the water; "We will not estimate a volume or speculate on a cause until we have facts." Did not name the vessels or terminal.
Not named on day 0: the unidentified terminal operator issued a brief written statement saying it had reported a discharge from two vessels at its berth and was working with authorities.
Filed the national landfall-and-spill story datelined Corpus Christi (arc beat: hurricane and spill national story).
To the national wire on landfall day: "This was a dangerous storm, and it did what we warned it would do. Today the water is the story."

Landfall day: called the in-harbor spill "a different animal" from a storm pause; said buyers would watch channel condition, dock and tank-farm damage, and any Inner Harbor limits; "Corpus is the swing barrel for a lot of export books."

Landfall day: added "heard from / not heard from" columns to her penciled binder of neighbors; "I'm not judging anybody. I'm counting them"; told her deacons nobody goes out in the wind, "Tomorrow, we walk"; "First you find everybody. Then you feed everybody."

Rode out Rafael at home on North Beach; with both bridges closed: "I can see downtown from my porch, and I can't get to it... We're an island this morning"; has water, a few days of food and a good radio (consistent with his "water, a radio and a ladder" plan).

Day after landfall, on 911 volume (about 2,900 calls a day, nearly ten times normal): "Every one of those calls is somebody's worst night"; urged non-emergency lines for non-urgent problems; "Every car out there sightseeing is a car in the way of a crew."

Day after landfall: said many people finding her had no charged phone; "When they need help, they knock on a door. Sometimes it's mine"; began walking the neighborhood with volunteers Wednesday, writing down who needs water, food or medicine.

Unified Command briefing (arc beat): about 9,000 barrels from MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth; priorities are public and responder safety and sensitive shoreline; "We will put crews on the water as soon as the winds allow it. We are not there yet"; Navy salvage equipment requested (type and timing not given); cause under investigation.

First appearance: GLO will focus first on keeping oil out of marshes once boats and boom can go out; "Shoreline is where a spill gets slow and expensive. The sooner we get boom in the water, the more shoreline we save."

First named statement (arc beat): Rendal Terminals "cooperating fully" with the Unified Command; "Our first concern is the safety of everyone at our facility and in the surrounding community"; "inappropriate to speculate about the cause while the investigation is underway."
To the national wire: "The weather is still setting the pace. We will be on the water as soon as it is safe."
To the national wire: "We are still in rescue-and-assess mode. Nobody should be out sightseeing."
Day 1: said Coastline plans to compare the flood footprint with census income and vehicle-access data (sets up later tract analysis).

First appearance in the storm: explained radar flood imaging (smooth water shows dark) and a shallow-pan analogy for surge; on day 1 declined to guess where the oil had gone: "Wind and water level decide that, and both are still changing."

Arc beat (shop gutted): evacuated the island before Rafael, did not ride out a third storm; got first look at the shop Wednesday; waterline above his head; building and walls standing, roof "mostly there," labeled plywood held on the windows but interior is "a do-over"; freezer in the parking lot; plans to start shoveling Thursday; "Somebody's going to want bait eventually."

Ran a storm special for base families the day after landfall: water conservation, bridge closures, aircraft still at NAS JRB Fort Worth; urged readers to rely on official channels because "storms bring rumors."
Wrote the oil-in-the-marshes story on day 2 (her arc beat lists day 1, but the public record makes it public on day 2).

Day 2, oil ashore: "We've got oil on sand, oil on rock and oil in the grass... You can rake a beach. You can't rake a marsh without killing it"; announced boom deployment as winds dropped and the wildlife hotline.
Arc beat (oil on North Beach): smelled oil before he saw it, thought a generator was leaking; sand "black at the edge"; "I've never seen this beach like that."
Day 2: explained surge lifting oil out of the harbor; "it left the oil behind like a bathtub ring. Except the bathtub is a marsh full of nursery habitat for shrimp, crabs and redfish."
Wildlife hotline guidance: "If you see an oiled animal, don't chase it and don't try to wash it. Call it in, note exactly where it is and let trained people handle it."

Arc beat (waits for help): rode out Rafael at home with her three kids in the house she rents near the bay; no car, couldn't line up a ride; water stopped a few inches below her door (homes a block closer to the bay flooded); fewer than a dozen water bottles left Thursday; no power; hasn't seen any agency on her street; can't reach two elderly clients by phone; "Ni modo. We stayed, we prayed and we're still here"; "Ask me again in three days."
Walking the neighborhood with volunteers since Wednesday: "Rosa's on my list. So is half this street. We're getting to everybody."
First rumor fact-check, day 2 (home-seizure and wealthy-only aid claims labeled false in the headline).
On the aid rumor: "Nobody is sorting neighborhoods by income to decide who gets help. If you need help, ask for it. Don't let a post talk you out of it."

First viral rumor (arc beat): posts claiming the military is seizing storm-damaged homes ("WATCH YOUR DOORS," "they don't want you to know") and that aid is only for wealthy areas; debunked by Harborline 6, no evidence offered.
Day 2: "Our crews are on the water now that conditions allow it. Shoreline protection is the priority"; cause still under investigation, "we will not speculate on it."
First story on the lights over the air station (day 2); NAS did not immediately respond.

Arc beat (first video posted): filmed a few lights hovering over NAS Corpus Christi on Wednesday night (day 1) from Flour Bluff while city lights were out; posted the clip Thursday; logged them as "unknown"; noticed the quiet since the training aircraft left ("This week, nothing. Then these"); will keep filming with time and direction noted.
Bridges reopen: "Both bridges passed inspection. Open doesn't mean normal. Drive slow, watch for crews and give yourself extra time."
Bridges reopen Friday morning: among the first in line off North Beach; "Felt like getting let out of jail"; first errand groceries; his water-radio-ladder plan worked, never needed the ladder.
Arc beat: fact-check "No, the military is not seizing homes," with county and NAS officials; also addressed refinery-blame posts.
Day 3 rumor control: "There is no truth to it. Nobody's home is being taken. Our people live here too. They're your neighbors."
Day 3 rumor control (arc beat): "If somebody knocks on your door saying they're from the government and they're taking your house, ask for identification and call us. No one is taking homes."
Kept posting home-seizure claims after the day-2 debunk.
Spill-blame posts (arc beat): claims refinery negligence caused the spill, blaming "the brass and the refineries"; fact-checked: cause under investigation, no agency has tied it to a refinery.
To Anchor & Rotor: "That rumor is false, full stop. No one's home is being taken."

Damage update (arc beat): depot hangar roof damage and water intrusion; workers told to stand by for word from supervisors; "Our workforce is the heart of this depot"; did not detail extent of damage.
Picked up water, bread and rice at Whitfield's hub on Friday; volunteers had checked on one of her elderly clients, who was OK: "That's the best thing anybody's told me all week."

Arc beat (hub opens before official aid): fellowship hall handing out bread, canned beans, diapers and water Friday, line before 8 a.m.; drew on the storage closet she stocked over the summer; "Nobody asked us to do this, and nobody needed to"; water is "the one thing I can't make"; "We'll be here when the trucks come. We'll be here when they leave."

First appearance: her ER is seeing burning throats, watery eyes, headaches and rashes from people near oiled shorelines; most go home; asthma/COPD patients should take it seriously; staff ask breathing patients where they live; urged people to bring a medication list or photo of pill bottles.

Arc beat (why the timing made it worse): cup-and-bucket analogy; marsh cleanup is a judgment call "acre by acre"; declined to discuss cause ("That's not my question to answer. My question is where it went"); shallow warm water may speed breakdown, "It's not a silver lining. It's just physics."
Arc beat (boil-water announcement): citywide notice issued Saturday; apologized again ("we're sorry"); "But this is not optional. Boil your water until we tell you it's safe."
Arc beat: boil-water notice explainer (day 4).
Boil-water explainer: crews "working around the clock at the plant"; "We'll lift it when testing tells us the water is safe, and not a day before."
First appearance: boil-water guidance ("Don't swallow water that hasn't been boiled"; rolling boil two minutes; hand-washing; watch the youngest and oldest); no illness signal reported yet.
On the fishing closure: "we are not going to let oiled seafood reach anybody's table. The closure stays until testing shows it's safe."

Arc beat (oil on his nets): boat survived the storm; ran a test drag in Corpus Christi Bay Friday (day 3) and pulled up a net streaked with oil, logged it in his spiral trip notebook; has a boat note, a fuel bill and a deckhand; "My father fished these bays. I fish these bays. I'll fish them again. I just don't know when."

One week into the closure: "Now it's how responders want to manage traffic through oiled water... That's a slower conversation"; "Nobody is going to rush tankers through a spill zone to save a few days."
Day 4 on reopening: "Reopening the channel is a safety decision. It will happen when the waterway is safe for traffic and for the response, and not before."

Day 4: 40 relief containers booked on Gulf Provider can't move while the channel is shut; "none of it matters until I've got water to bring a ship through"; exploring overland options, "Plan B for forty boxes on a ship is a lot of trucks I don't have."
Relayed the city's phishing warning to county residents: "If an email shows up out of nowhere telling you to log in to get your storm aid, stop. Don't click." (No link to rumors stated.)
Responding to Calallen residents' frustration: "they deserve straight answers... we will lift the notice when testing shows the water is safe."

Arc beat (water distribution line): waited more than an hour at a city distribution site Saturday, then made three more trips for elderly, sick and car-less neighbors; Sunday organized a street group-chat rotation; keeps a two-page clipboard list on the dash of her SUV; frustrated: "I need to know when, and nobody will tell me when"; "This week, this is my class."
Arc beat: respiratory complaints near the spill follow-up (day 5).

Respiratory and skin guidance near the spill: crude vapors irritate eyes, nose, throat and lungs; symptoms ease away from exposure; vulnerable groups listed; pairs oil avoidance with the boil-water notice ("Don't put something in your body that doesn't belong there"). Visit counts not released.
Day 5: spill-related complaints "every shift"; "the first thing they tell me is where they live."
Wrote a Sunday opinion column (day 5) arguing official supplies should go to the church hubs that fed people first; cites Whitfield and Rosa Elizondo.
Cited in Treviño's column: "nobody asked her church to do this, and nobody needed to."

Weekly roundup, day 5: boil water, city phishing warning (relayed only), depot standby, bridges open, oil and fishing closure, home-seizure rumor false; noted readers asking about lights over the station and that NAS had not commented publicly as of Sunday.
